text:
maya: Heads-up — infra CI for gpu-provisioning is flaky again, ~30% of runs failing on terraform apply with a state lock timeout. Seen across gha runners and self-hosted.
sam: ugh. any recent workflow changes? concurrency/group config? :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
maya: nope, no recent changes. failing logs show:
```
Error: Error acquiring the state lock: timeout while waiting to acquire lock (ID: xxxx)
```
jon: our self-hosted runner pool is saturated during nightly runs because the e2e/spot-node tests spin up GPU nodes. Runners queue and workflows overlap, so multiple applies race for the same workspace.
anya: can we split heavy e2e into a separate workflow that uses a different concurrency group + different runner label? keep apply jobs single-threaded.
lucas: also adding an explicit retry wrapper around apply helps for transient lock timeouts. use actions/toolkit or the community retry action.
maya: idea: use concurrency:
```
concurrency:
  group: "infra-terraform-${{ github.ref }}"
  cancel-in-progress: false
```
but that groups by ref which still allows parallel PRs to collide on the same backend workspace.
sam: we should group by workspace name instead (workspace id is in terraform backend config). can we compute workspace from path and use that in the group?
anja: (typo: anya) I can hack a small action to hash the backend key into the concurrency group.
ci-bot: [workflow-run] run_id=987654321 status=failure exit_code=1 steps=apply
ci-bot: logs snippet:
```
running terraform apply -auto-approve
Error: Failed to lock state: state locked by run 12345 (held by runner-3); try again later
```
jon: I also noticed helm lint inside the same workflow flakes intermittently because kubeconfig access times out while cluster is spinning up. maybe move helm lint after the cluster is ready or mock it in unit tests.
lucas: another optimisation — for provider/plugin downloads we should persist plugin cache between runs (actions/cache) so init is faster and less likely to hit transient network failures.
maya: rolling plan: 1) split heavy e2e/gpu spinups into separate workflow on different runner label 2) change concurrency group to include backend workspace id 3) add small retry-wrapper (3 retries, linear backoff) for terraform apply 4) persist terraform plugin cache via actions/cache 5) move helm lint to later stage or mark non-blocking
sam: +1. also add diagnostics in the apply step to dump who holds the lock when it happens (so we can detect leaks): `terraform force-unlock -force` should be avoided but helpful for debugging.
anya: I'll open a PR to update .github/workflows/infra.yml with the concurrency change and cache. will also add a note in the README to avoid broad workspace sharing across repos.
infra-bot: scheduled job created: nightly-cleanup/release-locks (disabled by default) — requires manual review before enabling.
maya: thanks — if you can include a tiny script that checks dynamodb (our backend) for orphaned locks that would be great.
jon: small follow-up: consider adding `persisted-runners` pool for GPU tests to reduce spin-up noise on shared runners.
lucas: FYI we observed one run where docker layer cache miss increased init time by 7m which bumped into the default gha job timeout; increasing timeouts for heavy infra jobs is reasonable.
maya: cool — let's iterate. I'll tag owners on the PR and we can gate the infra repo until we land the concurrency fix.
sam: thanks team. ping me if CI still flaky after changes and we'll throttle concurrent PR runs for a bit.
maya: closing loop — created PR #1428, running test matrix on feature branch now. will update thread once we have green runs. :thumbsup:
